name: Slow Cooker Kung Pao Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3200 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/4-1/2 tsp (3 g)
steps: Drop the chicken, soy sauce, honey, hoisin, olive oil, and garlic into the slow cooker and stir to coat.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is fall-apart tender.
Add the diced green bell peppers and zucchini for the last 45 minutes so they keep a little bite.
Whisk the cornstarch with cold water, stir it in, and let the sauce cook down and thicken for 20 minutes.
Shred the chicken into the sauce and spoon it over hot white rice.

name: Slow Cooker Maple Dijon Pork Bowls
steps: Place the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker.
Stir the sugar-free maple syrup, dijon mustard, and garlic powder together, then pour it over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is fork tender.
Steam the green beans just until crisp-tender near the end.
Roast or boil the potatoes until soft.
Slice or shred the pork, serve it over potatoes, and add the green beans on the side.

name: Slow Cooker Mediterranean Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3450 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Add the chicken, sliced onion, chicken broth, olive oil, garlic, and lime juice to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender all the way through.
Stir in the chopped roasted red peppers and olives during the last 30 minutes.
Shred the chicken into the pot so it soaks up the savory, briny juices.
Serve over white rice with plenty of the peppers and olives spooned on top.

name: Slow Cooker Mississippi Pork Bowls
ingredients: Ranch Seasoning Mix (Hidden Valley): 1 packet (36 g)
Au Jus Gravy Mix: 1 (1 oz) packet (65 g)
steps: Set the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker and surround it with the potatoes and shredded carrots.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix over everything.
Add the pepperoncini along with a splash of their juice, then lay the butter on top.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork and potatoes are tender.
Shred the pork and stir it through all those buttery, tangy juices.
Divide the pork and potatoes into your containers.

name: Slow Cooker Mongolian Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3400 g)
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, brown sugar, hoisin, sesame oil, and garlic in the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken shreds with almost no effort.
Stir in the broccoli florets during the final 30 minutes so they cook through but stay green.
If you want a thicker sauce, spoon a little off, whisk in a pinch of cornstarch, and stir it back in.
Pull the chicken apart in the pot and serve over steaming white rice.

name: Slow Cooker Orange Chicken Rice Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3100 g)
steps: Add the chicken breast and minced garlic to the crock.
Pour in the orange juice, soy sauce, honey, and a splash of sesame oil.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, then whisk the cornstarch with a little water and stir it in to thicken the sauce.
Steam the broccoli and cook the rice.
Serve the orange chicken over rice with broccoli.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Birria Bowls
ingredients: Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 2.3 cans (463 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 28 oz (791 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the pork shoulder, season it with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, ground cumin and dried oregano, and sear it hard in the vegetable oil in batches.
Add the seared pork to the slow cooker with the diced onion, minced garlic, the chipotles in adobo, the chicken broth and the bay leaves.
Cook on low for 8 hours, until the pork falls apart when you press it with a spoon.
Lift the meat out and shred it, then skim the red fat off the top of the braising liquid and save that fat separately. Keep the rest of the liquid as your consomme.
Dip each tortilla in the reserved red fat, lay it on a hot griddle, add shredded pork and the Mexican cheese blend, fold it over, and crisp both sides.
Stir the lime juice into the consomme and chop the cilantro to scatter over everything at the end.

name: Pork Carnitas Burrito Bowl
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (420 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): freshly cracked (4 g)
Ground Cinnamon (Great Value): 2 small sticks (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rub the pork loin all over with cumin, chili powder, onion powder, and a little salt and pepper. Set it in the slow cooker and add the minced garlic, lime juice, and fresh orange juice.
Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours, or on high for 4 to 5 hours, until the pork is fork-tender.
About an hour before it is done, shred the pork right in the pot with two forks and let it soak up the citrusy juices.
For crispy edges, spread the shredded pork on a foil-lined baking sheet and broil for 8 to 10 minutes. Watch it closely so it browns without burning.
Cook the rice per the package. Warm and drain the black beans and the corn.
In your weighed pot, combine the rice, beans, corn, and crisped pork, then fold in the fat free cheddar so it melts into the warm mix.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Green Chili Bowls
ingredients: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 7 cans (760 g)
Green Chile Sauce: 16 oz jar (680 g)
steps: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker with the chopped onion.
Pour in the diced green chiles and salsa verde.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it through the green chili sauce.
Let it simmer uncovered for a few minutes if you want the sauce a little thicker.
Serve over cooked white rice and divide into containers.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Posole Verde Bowls
ingredients: Dried Oregano (Great Value): 1 jar (Mexican oregano) (4 g)
steps: Set the pork loin in the slow cooker with the chopped onion.
Add the tomatillos, poblano peppers, and enough water to nearly cover.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is tender.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it back through the broth.
Stir in the drained hominy and cook another 20 to 30 minutes to warm through.
Ladle into bowls, hominy and all, and portion into containers.

name: Slow Cooker Pork and Sauerkraut with Apples and Potatoes
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the pork loin dry, season it all over with salt and black pepper, and sear it in the vegetable oil in a hot skillet until the outside is browned on every side.
Lay the sliced onion in the bottom of the slow cooker and set the seared pork on top of it.
Drain the sauerkraut, rinse it if you prefer it mild, and pile it around and over the pork along with the minced garlic.
Core and slice the apples and tuck them in around the edges, then pour the apple juice over everything.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours, until the pork pulls apart easily with a fork.
Shred the pork right in the crock so it takes the juices back up, and cook the rice per the package to serve underneath.

name: Slow Cooker Pork Tinga Bowls
ingredients: Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 1 can (90 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (7 g)
steps: Add the pork loin, sliced onions, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and stir in the chopped chipotle in adobo.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds with a fork.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it back into the smoky sauce.
Cook the rice while the pork soaks up the flavor.
Spoon the saucy pork over the rice and serve.

name: Classic Slow Cooker Pot Roast with Potatoes and Carrots
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pat the chuck roast dry, season it heavily with salt and black pepper, and sear it in the olive oil in a hot pan until it is deeply browned on all sides.
Move the roast to the slow cooker. In the same pan, cook the chopped onion and garlic until soft, scraping the browned bits loose.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute, then whisk in the beef broth until it is smooth and starting to thicken.
Pour that over the roast, then add the carrots, celery, potatoes, thyme, and Italian seasoning around it.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the roast pulls apart with light pressure from a fork.
Lift the roast out, shred it, and stir it back into the vegetables and gravy.
Taste the gravy and correct the salt. Long cooks dull seasoning, so it almost always needs a little at the end.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork Rice Bowl
ingredients: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 bottle (450 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 4 cans (840 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (common in rub) (4 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Trim the pork tenderloin of any silverskin and excess fat, then lay it in the slow cooker. Pour in the chicken broth and season with garlic powder and onion powder, plus a little salt and pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours, or on high for 3 to 4 hours, until the pork pulls apart with almost no effort.
Lift the pork out and shred it with two forks. Skim off most of the cooking liquid, then return the meat to the pot with a splash of that liquid to keep it juicy.
Stir in the sugar-free BBQ sauce until every strand is coated.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the package. Drain and warm the sweet corn.
Combine the rice, corn, and saucy pork in your weighed pot and fold everything together.

name: Slow Cooker Ranch Pork and Potato Bowls
ingredients: Ranch Seasoning Mix (Hidden Valley): 1 packet (27 g)
steps: Rub the pork loin with a little olive oil and set it in the slow cooker.
Add the potatoes and shredded carrots around the pork.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix over everything and dot the top with butter.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork and potatoes are tender.
Shred the pork and stir it through the buttery ranch juices.
Divide the pork, potatoes, and carrots into your containers.

name: Slow Cooker Root Beer Pulled Pork Bowls
ingredients: BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 bottle (300 g)
steps: Add the pork tenderloin, sliced onion, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Pour in the zero-sugar soda and half the barbecue sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart easily.
Shred the pork, drain off most of the liquid, and stir in the rest of the barbecue sauce.
Roast or boil the potatoes until fork tender.
Pile the pulled pork over the potatoes and top with the shredded cabbage for crunch.

name: Slow Cooker Salsa Chicken Burrito Bowl
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2495 g)
Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 1 can (113 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans (910 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Place the chicken breast in the bottom of the slow cooker and sprinkle the taco seasoning over the top.
Add the can of diced green chiles and pour the salsa over everything so the chicken is covered.
Cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 3 hours, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Shred the chicken with two forks and stir it back into the salsa so every piece soaks up the flavor.
Cook the rice, drain and warm the black beans, and add both to your empty weighed mixing pot.
Fold the salsa chicken into the rice and beans, then stir in the fat free cheddar until it melts through.

name: Salsa Verde Chicken Burrito Bowl
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2495 g)
Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 4 cans (910 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (420 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (196 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (3 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.

Put the chicken breast in the slow cooker, sprinkle on the cumin and a little salt, then pour most of the salsa verde over the top. Save a little for the end. Cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or high for about 3, until the chicken shreds easily.
While it cooks, make your rice per the package. This is the base that carries the whole batch.
Drain and rinse the black beans and drain the corn, then warm them through in a pan or the microwave.

Shred the chicken right in the slow cooker with two forks, then stir in the reserved salsa verde and a good squeeze of lime juice. Adding the salsa at the end keeps it saucy and fresh instead of cooked down.
Fold the cooked rice, warm beans, and corn into your weighed mixing pot along with the chicken.
Stir in the fat free cheddar to taste and mix until everything is evenly combined.

name: Slow Cooker Salsa Verde Pork Bowls
ingredients: Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 2 cans (120 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 3 cans (750 g)
steps: Set the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker.
Pour the salsa verde, diced green chiles, and chicken broth over the top.
Add a squeeze of lime juice and the minced garlic.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart easily.
Shred the pork and stir it back into all those juices, then fold in the corn.
Spoon over cooked white rice and divide into containers.

name: Slow Cooker Sauerbraten Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Combine the red wine vinegar with the sliced onion, cloves, bay leaves, salt, and pepper. Submerge the chuck roast in it and refrigerate overnight, turning it once if you think of it.
Lift the roast out and pat it dry, keeping the marinade. Sear it in the vegetable oil until it is browned on all sides.
Set the roast in the slow cooker, pour in the strained marinade along with the beef broth, and add the minced garlic.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the beef shreds with no effort.
Lift the roast out and shred it. Whisk the flour into a little cold water and stir it into the hot liquid.
Crush the gingersnaps fine and whisk them in with the brown sugar. Cook on high 15 to 20 minutes until the gravy goes thick and glossy.
Return the shredded beef to the gravy and cook the rice separately.

name: Slow Cooker Steak and Onions over Rice
ingredients: Brown Gravy Mix (generic dry (USDA)): 2 oz (58 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the steaks with salt, black pepper, and Italian seasoning and lay them in the slow cooker in an even layer.
Slice the onions thick and pile them over the steaks along with the minced garlic.
Whisk the brown gravy mix with about two cups of water and pour it over everything.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, until the steaks are tender and the onions have collapsed into the gravy.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little cold water, stir it into the hot liquid, and cook on high 15 to 20 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Break the steaks into large pieces in the gravy and let them sit in it for 10 minutes.
Cook the rice separately and keep it plain so the gravy carries the plate.

name: Slow Cooker Sweet and Sour Pork Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1 tsp (8 g)
steps: Add the pork tenderloin, sliced peppers, and onion to the slow cooker.
Stir the honey, soy sauce, and pineapple with its juice together, then pour it over the top.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the pork is tender.
Cook the rice while the pork finishes.
Cut or shred the pork into bite-sized pieces and stir it back through the sauce.
Spoon the pork and vegetables over rice and drizzle with extra sauce.

name: Slow Cooker Swiss Steak with Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck roast into thick slabs or large cubes, season them with salt and black pepper, and dredge each piece in the flour.
Brown the dredged beef in the vegetable oil in batches over medium high heat. Do not crowd the pan or the flour will go gummy instead of golden.
Move the browned beef to the slow cooker and scatter the sliced onion, sliced bell peppers, and minced garlic over it.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice, the beef broth, and the Worcestershire sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 7 hours, until the beef is fork tender and the sauce has thickened from the flour on the meat.
Break the beef into large pieces in the sauce, then taste and correct the salt and pepper.
Cook the rice separately and serve the beef and sauce over it.

name: Slow Cooker Teriyaki Pork Bowls
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 1/2 tsp red chili pepper flakes (2 g)
steps: Place the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker and scatter the sliced onion around it.
Pour the teriyaki sauce, chicken broth, honey, and garlic over the top.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork pulls apart.
Shred the pork and stir it back into the sauce with the onions.
Steam the broccoli florets until just tender.
Serve over cooked white rice and divide into containers.

name: Slow Cooker Thai Peanut Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3400 g)
steps: Add the chicken, peanut butter, coconut milk, chicken broth, soy sauce, honey, and garlic to the slow cooker and stir.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender and the sauce is glossy.
Stir in the sliced red bell pepper for the last 45 minutes so it softens but holds its shape.
Whisk the sauce smooth, then shred the chicken right back into it.
Serve over white rice and spoon extra sauce on top.

name: Slow Cooker Turkey and Dumplings
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside. It goes under the stew in the containers.
Put the diced onion, sliced carrots, sliced celery and minced garlic in the slow cooker with the chicken broth, dried thyme, Italian seasoning, salt and black pepper.
Add the cooked turkey breast, put the lid on, and cook on low for 5 to 6 hours until the vegetables are tender and the broth tastes like a real stock.
Whisk together the flour, baking powder and salt, then cut in the softened butter and stir in the milk until you have a thick, sticky batter.
Turn the slow cooker to high, drop spoonfuls of the batter across the surface of the stew, and put the lid back on.
Cook 45 to 60 minutes without lifting the lid, until a dumpling comes out clean on a toothpick and the stew has thickened underneath.

name: Slow Cooker Turkey Chili Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 6 cans (2391 g)
Chipotle in Adobo (La Costena): 1 can (60 g)
Vegetable Oil (Great Value): for frying (~1 tbsp) (24 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Add the raw ground turkey to the slow cooker and break it up with a spoon.
Dump in the black beans, diced tomatoes, tomato paste, chopped onion, and bell peppers.
Stir in the chili powder and the chopped chipotle in adobo for a little smoky heat.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours, giving it one stir partway through if you are around.
Break up any big pieces of turkey, then serve it over or alongside more beans.

name: Slow Cooker Turkey Pasta e Fagioli
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 13 oz dry (368 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in a skillet, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F. A slow cooker will never brown meat, so this ten minutes on the stove is what keeps the soup from tasting flat.
Add the minced garlic to the pan for one minute, then scrape everything into the slow cooker.
Add the diced tomatoes, the beef broth, the dried basil, oregano, salt, and black pepper, and stir it together.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or on high for 3.
Add the diced zucchini and the drained cannellini beans in the last 45 minutes, so the zucchini stays intact and the beans do not turn to paste.
Cook the pasta shells separately in salted water, drain them, and toss them with a drizzle of oil so they do not clump in the fridge.
Taste the soup for salt, then move the pasta into your weighed pot.

name: Slow Cooker Turkey Zuppa Toscana
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Slice the smoked turkey sausage into coins and brown them in the olive oil in a skillet. Browning takes ten minutes and it is the single biggest flavor step in this recipe, so do not skip it just because a slow cooker is involved.
Move the sausage into the slow cooker, then cook the diced onion and minced garlic in the same skillet for 5 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, and add those too.
Cut the potatoes into half-inch thick slices and add them to the cooker with the chicken broth, the italian seasoning, cayenne, salt, and black pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 6 hours, or on high for 3, until the potatoes are completely tender and starting to soften at the edges.
Stir in the chopped kale and cook 15 minutes more, just long enough for it to wilt and turn deep green.
Turn the cooker off, then stir in the heavy cream. Adding it at the end and off the boil is what keeps it from separating into curds.
Let it stand 10 minutes to thicken, then move it into your weighed pot.

name: Slow Cooker Tuscan Chicken Pasta
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3300 g)
steps: Add the chicken, chopped sun-dried tomatoes, coconut milk, and chicken broth to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender and the sauce is fragrant.
Shred the chicken and stir in the parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil until the sauce turns creamy.
Boil the penne separately until just al dente and drain it.
Toss the pasta with the creamy Tuscan sauce, or spoon the sauce over each serving of pasta.

name: Slow Cooker White Chicken Chili Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3100 g)
steps: Add the chicken breast, chopped onion, and diced bell peppers to the crock.
Pour in both cans of coconut milk.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, then stir in the drained cannellini beans.
Let it warm through and thicken for another 20 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and dig in.

name: Smothered Chicken Thighs with Onion Gravy
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7 lb (3175 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Mix the flour with the cajun seasoning, paprika, cayenne, onion powder, garlic powder, thyme, salt, and pepper. Dredge the chicken thighs in it and shake off the excess. Keep the leftover seasoned flour, because that is your roux.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy skillet and brown the chicken on both sides until it has real color. Set it aside. It does not need to be cooked through.
Add the butter to the same pan and cook the sliced onions over medium heat until they are deep golden, about 15 minutes. Patience here is the whole recipe.
Add the garlic, then sprinkle in the reserved seasoned flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste. This is a roux and it will scorch if you walk away.
Whisk in the chicken broth a little at a time so no lumps form, then the milk, and bring it to a gentle simmer until it thickens.
Return the chicken and any juices, cover, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy coats a spoon.
Cook the rice and taste the gravy for salt before portioning.

name: Sopa de Fideo con Carne Molida (Mexican Beef and Noodle Skillet)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Break the spaghetti into pieces roughly an inch long.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large wide pot and toast the broken pasta over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it turns golden brown. Watch it closely, because it goes from perfect to burnt in about thirty seconds.
Scoop the toasted pasta out and set it aside.
Add the ground beef to the same pot and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the onion powder, garlic powder, dried oregano, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper and cook for a minute.
Add the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, and chicken broth and bring it to a boil.
Return the toasted pasta, lower the heat, and simmer uncovered until the noodles are tender and the liquid has cooked down to a thick sauce rather than a soup.

name: Soto Betawi (Indonesian Beef and Coconut Soup)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into bite sized pieces and simmer them in water with the lemongrass paste, bay leaves, and salt for about 90 minutes, until tender. Keep every bit of that broth.
While the beef cooks, blend most of the onion with the garlic, cashews, and ginger into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the vegetable oil over medium heat until it darkens and smells nutty rather than raw, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir the fried paste into the beef pot, then add the coconut milk and the milk. Keep it at a bare simmer so the coconut milk does not break.
Add the diced potato and simmer 15 to 20 minutes until it is soft but still holding its shape.
Add the tomatoes near the end so they stay in pieces, then finish with the lime juice and a heavy hand of black pepper.
Slice the green onions and the remaining onion thin for scattering over each bowl at serving.

name: South African Bobotie (Curried Beef Custard Bake)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Tear the sandwich bread into pieces and soak it in most of the milk until it goes soft, then squeeze it out and set the milk aside.
Melt the butter in a large pot and cook the diced yellow onions until deeply softened and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, ground turmeric, and black pepper and cook for a minute so the spices bloom in the fat.
Add the ground beef, break it up, and cook until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the honey, golden raisins, white vinegar, worcestershire sauce, beef broth, the soaked bread, and salt, then simmer until the mixture is thick and no longer soupy.
Spread the beef into a large greased baking dish, press it flat, and tuck the bay leaves into the surface.
Whisk the eggs with the reserved milk and the heavy cream, pour that custard over the beef, and bake at 350 degrees until the top is set and golden.

name: South Indian Chettinad Pepper Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 6.25 lb (2800 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Finely chop the onions and mince the garlic and ginger. There is a lot of onion here on purpose, it cooks down into the body of the sauce.
Cook the onions in a large pot over medium heat until deeply golden, 12 to 15 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger and cook 2 more minutes.
Add the black pepper, ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, chili powder, and Italian seasoning and toast in the onions for 1 minute until fragrant.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite-size pieces and add them with the salt. Stir to coat in the masala, then cover and simmer, stirring now and then, until the chicken hits 165F.
Stir in the Dijon mustard and sugar, then simmer uncovered until the sauce thickens and clings to the chicken.
Serve the pepper chicken over the rice.

name: Southern Smothered Pork Chops and Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Season the pork chops with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne, then dredge them in the flour. Save the leftover seasoned flour, that is your gravy starter.
Fry the chops in vegetable oil over medium-high heat, about 4 minutes per side, until golden and 145F inside. Work in batches and set them on a plate.
Pour off all but a few tablespoons of the oil, then cook the onions in the drippings until soft and browned at the edges. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in a few spoonfuls of the reserved seasoned flour and cook 1 to 2 minutes, then whisk in the chicken broth slowly so it stays smooth. Simmer until it thickens into gravy.
Stir in the heavy cream, return the chops, and let them smother in the gravy for 10 minutes on low.
Serve the chops and gravy over the rice.

name: Southwestern Turkey Rice Casserole
ingredients: Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 2.3 cans (660 g)
Diced Green Chiles (Old El Paso): 2.3 cans (264 g)
Cream of Chicken Soup (generic condensed (USDA)): 2.3 cans (695 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 18.5 oz (527 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt the butter in a large pot, cook the diced onion 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the dry rice and toast it for two minutes.
Add one can of the tomatoes with green chilies plus enough water to cook the rice, season with the ground cumin and salt, then cover and simmer 18 minutes until tender.
Thaw the frozen chopped spinach and wring it dry in a clean towel. Squeeze harder than feels necessary, then squeeze once more.
In a large bowl, stir together the light sour cream, the condensed cream of chicken soup, the remaining tomatoes with green chilies, and the drained diced green chiles.
Fold in the chopped turkey breast, the squeezed spinach, the cooked Spanish rice, and about two thirds of the Mexican cheese blend, then season with salt and black pepper.
Spread everything into a greased 9x13 pan, top with the remaining cheese, and bake at 350F for 30 minutes until it bubbles at the edges.
Crush the corn chips over the top and return the pan for 5 minutes only, just long enough to warm them without letting them soften. Rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Spanish Turkey Albondigas over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook about a third of the rice and let it cool. This is the rice that goes inside the meatballs, so it has to be cooked before it gets mixed in.
Mix the ground turkey with the cooled rice, the eggs, half the minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, salt, and black pepper. Mix with a light hand and stop as soon as it comes together.
Roll it into small meatballs and set them on sheet pans. Bake at 400F for about 15 minutes to firm them up so they do not fall apart in the sauce.

While they bake, heat the olive oil in a wide pot, cook the rest of the garlic for a minute, then add the tomato sauce, chicken broth, red wine vinegar, more smoked paprika, a pinch of cayenne, and black pepper.
Slide the meatballs into the sauce, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until they reach 165F and the sauce has tightened up.
Stir in the heavy cream off the heat and taste for salt. It should look like tomato soup that went to finishing school.
Cook the remaining rice, move it into your weighed pot, and keep the meatballs in their sauce for portioning.

name: Spicy Italian Sausage Orzo
ingredients: Orzo Pasta (Great Value): 16.75 oz dry (476 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the fresh basil, holding the basil back until the very end.
Brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles in a large deep pot until it has color on it. Do not drain the fat, because that fat is going to season the orzo.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft, then the garlic and the dried oregano for a minute.
Pour in the tomato sauce and the chicken broth, scrape the bottom of the pot clean, and bring it up to a simmer.
Stir in the dry orzo and cook uncovered, stirring often. Orzo settles and scorches if you walk away from it, so stay close and keep the spoon moving.
When the orzo is tender and the liquid has thickened around it, turn the heat low and stir in the heavy cream and the parmesan.
Season with salt and black pepper, then fold in the chopped fresh basil off the heat so it stays bright.

name: Spicy Pork Noodles
ingredients: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 63.5 oz dry (1801 g)
Chili Crisp (Lao Gan Ma (Laoganma)): 7 tbsp (98 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the lo mein noodles until just al dente, drain, and toss with a small splash of oil so they do not clump.
Brown the ground pork in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up and letting it sit undisturbed a few minutes at a time so it gets crispy edges. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add the garlic and ginger to the pork and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the chili crisp, hoisin sauce, soy sauce, and lime juice and let it bubble for 2 minutes so the sauce coats the meat.
Add the noodles and most of the green onions and toss until every strand is glossy.
Finish with the toasted sesame seeds and the rest of the green onions.

name: Spicy Vodka Rigatoni with Italian Sausage
ingredients: Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 33.5 oz dry (953 g)
Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 4.25 tbsp (23 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, mince the garlic, and strip the kale leaves from their stems and tear them.
Boil the pasta in well salted water until just shy of tender, then reserve a mug of the starchy water before you drain it. That water is what makes the sauce cling later.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and brown the hot Italian sausage in crumbles until it has color, not just gray.
Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic and the red pepper flakes for a minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and keep stirring for three or four minutes until it darkens from bright red to brick. This step is the whole sauce, so do not rush it.
Pour in the heavy cream, stir until it turns a uniform blush color, then fold in the torn kale and let it wilt.
Add the drained pasta and the parmesan, splash in the reserved pasta water a little at a time, and toss until the sauce coats every piece.

name: Steak Fajita Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the olive oil, orange juice, lime juice, minced garlic, chopped cilantro, cumin, chili powder, oregano, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper into a marinade.
Slice the sirloin thin against the grain, toss it in the marinade, and let it sit at least 30 minutes while you cut the vegetables.
Slice the onions, poblanos, and bell peppers into strips of roughly the same thickness so they cook at the same rate.
Get a wide pan very hot with the vegetable oil and sear the beef in batches, about 90 seconds a side. Pull it out and set it aside.
In the same pan, cook the peppers and onions over high heat until they are charred at the edges but still have some bite.
Return the beef and any juices to the pan, toss everything together for 30 seconds, and kill the heat.
Cook the rice separately and keep the sour cream cold to spoon on at serving.

name: Sudado de Cerdo (Colombian Pork and Potato Stew)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the pork chops with salt, black pepper, ground cumin and the sazon seasoning, then brown them in the vegetable oil in a heavy pot, in batches, until both sides have color.
Cook the diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot until soft, scraping up whatever the pork left behind.
Add the diced tomatoes with their juice and let them cook down for about five minutes into a thick base.
Return the pork chops to the pot, tuck in the sliced carrots and the peeled and quartered potatoes, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for about an hour.
Resist adding water. The vegetables and tomato give off enough liquid to make the sauce, and that is where the flavor concentration comes from.
When the potatoes are fork tender, stir in the chopped green onions and cilantro and taste for salt. Cook the rice per the package to serve underneath.

name: Swedish Meatball and Potato Bowls
steps: Mix the ground beef with bread crumbs, a little milk, and grated onion, then roll into small meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in a large skillet until they are cooked through, working in batches if you need to.
Pour in the beef broth and let it simmer so the meatballs soak up the flavor.
Stir in the sour cream off the heat to build a smooth, creamy gravy.
Serve the meatballs and gravy over cooked potatoes and spoon extra sauce on top.

name: Szegedin Goulash (Pork and Sauerkraut Paprika Stew)
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (168 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the pork shoulder into large cubes and pat them dry. Dice the onions and the green bell peppers, and drain the sauerkraut.
Render the chopped bacon in a heavy pot until the fat runs, then brown the pork cubes in that fat in batches and set them aside.
Cook the onions and peppers in the pot until soft, then add the garlic for a minute.
Pull the pot off the heat before you stir in the paprika. Paprika scorches fast over direct heat and turns bitter, and that single step is what separates a good goulash from a ruined one.
Return the pot to the burner, add the diced tomatoes, beef broth, caraway seeds and bay leaves, and bring it to a simmer.
Return the pork, cover, and braise low until the meat is fork tender, then stir in the sauerkraut and cook another stretch so it softens into the sauce.
Kill the heat, temper the sour cream with a ladle of the hot liquid, then stir it back into the pot. Cook the rice separately to serve underneath.

name: Taiwanese Braised Beef Noodle Bowls
ingredients: Doubanjiang (Lee Kum Kee (Chili Bean Sauce Toban Djan)): 1.5 oz (45 g)
Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 44.75 oz dry (1270 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chuck into large chunks and blanch it in boiling water for a few minutes, then drain and rinse. This pulls out the scum and gives you a clear broth instead of a cloudy one.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and fry the ginger, garlic, yellow onion, and the white parts of the green onions until fragrant.
Stir in the doubanjiang, tomato paste, and dried arbol chiles and cook for a minute until the oil turns red.
Add the beef back with the diced tomatoes, soy sauce, chicken broth, sugar, and enough water to cover. Bring it to a simmer and skim off anything that rises.
Cover and simmer low for 2 to 3 hours, until the beef is tender enough to break with chopsticks. Taste the broth and adjust the salt at the end, not the beginning.
Cook the lo mein noodles just short of done, drain, and rinse them in cold water so they stop cooking and do not clump.
Divide the noodles into the containers, ladle the beef and broth over the top, and finish with the green onion tops and chopped cilantro.

name: Taiwanese Lu Rou Fan Pork Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Hand dice the pork shoulder into small pieces rather than grinding it. The texture of lu rou fan comes from distinct little cubes, not a paste.
Hard boil the eggs, cool them, and peel them so they are ready to go into the braise.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions until they turn deep golden and crisp at the edges, then lift most of them out and set them aside.
Brown the diced pork in that same oil until the pieces have color and the fat starts to render.
Add the garlic and the sugar and stir until the sugar melts and coats everything in a dark glaze, which takes only a minute or two and is the step that makes this dish look right.
Pour in the soy sauce and the chicken broth, add the sliced mushrooms, the five spice powder and the black pepper, then return the fried onions.
Add the peeled eggs, cover, and simmer very low until the pork is falling apart. Cook the rice and blanch the broccoli near the end so both are fresh.

name: Taiwanese Three Cup Chicken
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.5 lb (3360 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the chicken thighs into large bite sized pieces and pat them very dry.
Start the rice.

Heat the sesame oil and vegetable oil together in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the sliced ginger until the edges curl and go slightly crisp. Do not rush this, because that fried ginger is a signature of the dish.
Add the whole peeled garlic cloves and the dried arbol chiles and cook until the garlic turns golden. Whole cloves, not minced. They go sweet and soft during the braise.
Turn the heat up, add the chicken, and brown it on all sides.

Pour in the soy sauce, chicken broth, and sugar, bring it to a boil, then simmer uncovered 20 to 25 minutes while the sauce reduces down and turns glossy and dark. Stir now and then so nothing catches.
Kill the heat, throw in the entire pile of basil leaves, and stir just until they wilt. Ten seconds. Basil cooked any longer than that turns black and loses everything.

name: Teriyaki Chicken and Rice Bowl
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 6 lb (2495 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot on a kitchen scale and write the number down. You will need it to portion evenly at the end.
Rinse the rice, then cook it according to the package. Set it aside to steam while you handle the skillet.

Heat a splash of olive oil in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add the broccoli and shredded carrots and cook 5 to 6 minutes until the broccoli turns bright green and the carrots soften a little. Scoop the veggies into a bowl and set aside.
Dice the chicken breast into bite sized pieces. Add a little more oil to the hot skillet, then add the chicken in batches so it browns instead of steaming.
Cook the chicken until it is no longer pink in the center and reaches 165 degrees. Do not crowd the pan. Give it room to get a little color.
Return the veggies to the skillet and pour in the teriyaki sauce. Stir everything together and cook 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce coats every piece and the whole thing is hot.
Fold the cooked rice into the skillet, or layer it into your containers first. Either way works fine.
